routes.description: Establish that life-permitting fine-tuning raises the probability of classical theism relative to the specified single-universe naturalistic alternatives.
routes.successCriteria: The likelihood and intrinsic-probability comparisons must jointly make fine-tuning substantially less expected under the relevant naturalistic space than under classical theism.

motionBridge.description: Show that fine-tuning provides strong comparative confirmation of classical theism over specified single-universe naturalism.

centralBridges.description: Establish that life-permitting parameters are substantially more expected given a perfectly good creator than given single-universe naturalism.
Show that naturalistic hypotheses augmented to predict fine-tuning occupy little relevant probability space despite their fit with the observation.
Establish that the coherence or simplicity of perfect-being theism preserves enough intrinsic probability to support the comparative inference.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Explain why unrestricted naturalistic alternatives do not neutralize every possible empirical inference to theism.
Account for simulation and other naturalistic designer scenarios without merely relocating fine-tuning to an unexplained base reality.

routes.description: Undercut strong confirmation by challenging the likelihoods, hypothesis-space partition, intrinsic probabilities, and status of the fine-tuning datum.
routes.successCriteria: At least one indispensable comparative step must remain unjustified or sufficiently ambiguous that fine-tuning does not strongly discriminate in favor of God.

motionBridge.description: Show that fine-tuning does not securely yield strong comparative evidence for classical theism.

centralBridges.description: Challenge whether divine goodness supplies a justified prediction of a life-permitting or specifically fine-tuned universe.
Require comparison with the relevant naturalistic disjunction, including broad alien, simulation, and other naturalistic scenarios.
Challenge the assignment and aggregation of intrinsic probabilities across unlimited, limited, coherent, modest, and parsimonious hypotheses.
Show that competing theoretical virtues cannot be weighted precisely enough to support the asserted posterior comparison.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Preserve the possibility that apparently intentional phenomena receive unanticipated natural explanations.
Consider whether apparent fine-tuning indicates a defect of physical theory rather than an objective cosmic feature requiring design.

sectionSelections.title: Fine-Tuning as Data and the Theistic Likelihood
sectionSelections.rationale: The motion depends first on whether fine-tuning is an objective evidential datum and whether classical theism makes life-permitting conditions sufficiently expected.

proSelections.proposition: Fine-tuning confirms classical theism over single-universe naturalism because life-permitting parameters are far less surprising if a perfectly good creator wants conscious moral agents.

conSelections.proposition: Apparent fine-tuning may indicate a defect or instability in a physical theory rather than an objective feature of the universe requiring design.
Theistic likelihoods remain uncertain because divine goodness, its meaning, and the intentions or creative choices it would produce cannot simply be assumed.

sectionSelections.title: Scope and Granularity of the Comparison
sectionSelections.rationale: A comparative Bayesian inference requires a defined theistic hypothesis and a defined rival space whose members and level of specificity determine the relevant probabilities.

proSelections.proposition: The relevant comparison places classical perfect-being theism against every hypothesis consistent with a specified single-universe naturalism.

conSelections.proposition: Theism and naturalism are broad families, so a meaningful comparison must fix their granularity and compare the specified theism with the full relevant naturalistic disjunction.
Even restricted single-universe naturalism retains extensive resources such as aliens, time travel, and simulation, leaving a broad rival hypothesis space.

sectionSelections.title: Naturalistic Alternatives and Empirical Discrimination
sectionSelections.rationale: The force of fine-tuning evidence turns on whether available naturalistic auxiliaries legitimately diffuse the inference or instead generate unrestricted empirical skepticism.

proSelections.proposition: Allowing tailored naturalistic hypotheses to neutralize fine-tuning would likewise block every possible empirical inference to God and therefore proves too much.
If the same naturalistic-alternative strategy applies to every conceivable observation, it entails that no empirical evidence could ever raise the probability of theism.

conSelections.proposition: Apparently theistic evidence can admit alien, time-travel, and simulation explanations whose probabilities should be aggregated as a naturalistic disjunction.
Broad simulation and science-fiction possibilities give naturalism resources capable of accommodating extraordinary observations without decisively selecting theism.

sectionSelections.title: Agency, Motive, and Predictive Fit
sectionSelections.rationale: Evidence for intentional agency supports classical theism only if it also supplies justified information about the agent's goodness, purposes, and expected actions.

proSelections.proposition: Perfect goodness provides some basis for expectations about divine intentions, while tailoring an alien hypothesis to predict the evidence transfers improbability into its prior.

conSelections.proposition: Structured evidence can strongly indicate agency while providing much weaker evidence about the agent's benevolence, purposes, or identity.
General theism need not predict a particular religious event better than general alienism because both posit powerful agents whose specific intentions remain largely unknown.

sectionSelections.title: Coherence, Modesty, and Intrinsic Probability
sectionSelections.rationale: The inference requires an account of how probability is distributed among perfect-being theism, limited alternatives, and naturalism augmented to predict fine-tuning.

proSelections.proposition: Augmented naturalism occupies a negligible portion of naturalistic probability space, whereas perfect-being theism is a comparatively simple and substantial specification of design.
Even if limited quasi-theistic alternatives collectively exceed theism in probability, coherent theism can remain more probable than augmented naturalism, which lacks both coherence and modesty.

conSelections.proposition: The disjunction of all finite-limit hypotheses may have greater intrinsic probability than the single unlimited hypothesis despite the latter's relative simplicity.
The simplicity case for theism depends on an unresolved judgment about whether coherence or modesty dominates intrinsic probability.

sectionSelections.title: Parsimony and the Overall Probability Balance
sectionSelections.rationale: The motion-level conclusion requires integrating the claimed fine-tuning likelihood advantage with ontological parsimony and other theoretical virtues across the full comparison.

proSelections.proposition: Naturalism's ontological-simplicity advantage is modest enough to be outweighed by the larger coherence-based probability advantage of theism over augmented naturalism.
Coherence can outweigh disjunctive modesty, and the extremely low conditional probability of augmented naturalism can swamp naturalism's ontological-simplicity benefit.

conSelections.proposition: Naturalism gains ontological parsimony by positing natural reality alone, whereas theism adds a supernatural reality to the natural world.
Because parsimony and competing theoretical virtues cannot be reliably quantified or traded off, the posterior comparison remains reasonably ambiguous.
